title: RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture and Phase 4 acceptance run
description:
Phase 4 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign — the final acceptance gate.

Build a RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture in tests/fixtures/revengGraph.ts containing tmux_lib at tmux_lib, jfred/external/tmux_lib, and jfred/jfredToolsPlugin/external/tmux_lib; two occurrences each of claude_plugin_lib and scenarios; nested submodules beneath ordinary directories; and distinct parent chains. Drive a full run against it in tests/revengEndToEnd.test.ts.

Verify in that fixture that a change originating from any repeated occurrence converges everywhere; all child and ancestor suites pass; approval precedes every commit, merge, and push; all occurrence histories consolidate into one operation per logical repository; gitlinks propagate through the correct explicit parents to the root; and every intended local base ends at the expected merge commit. Also verify no semantic commit, push, integration merge, base mutation, or archival occurs before approval, and that only successfully published tasks are archived.

Phase 4 acceptance: the recursive workflow is the production path, completes the RevEng-shaped run without data loss, and archives only tasks whose integration was successfully published.
problemSolvedByTask: Without an end-to-end fixture spanning repeated nested submodules, nobody can trust the recursive discovery/merge system before it becomes the production path for every real multi-repo task.

title: Reorganize scripts/ into skillBodyGenerators/ plus topic subfolders, updating every reference
userDescription: organize the scripts folder: scripts that output skill bodies go in skillBodyGenerators/, everything else organized by topic (task/, git/, workflow/, etc).
description:
scripts/ now holds 96 .ts files, flat. Tasks 71-79 (the skillBodyGenerators/ split) are all closed, so that half of this task is done; the only remaining skill-body-generator file is scripts/reviewPlanBrief.ts, not worth its own folder for one file.

The real remaining value: reorganize scripts/ to follow the same pattern tackle-tasks' own scripts already use — scripts/tackle-tasks/<blockName>/ holds one folder per pipeline block (areTestsFlagged/, codexReviewsPlan/, implementTask/, planTheTask/, shared/, etc). Every other skill should get its own scripts/<skillName>/ folder holding all the source files that skill's hook and skill body use — not generic topic categories like task/ or git/. Scope is every source file used by any skill or hook, not just the 9 files hooks.json names directly: skills/*/SKILL.md reference many more flat scripts.ts files at the top level (e.g. scripts/clarifyTaskBrief.ts, scripts/rateTask.ts, scripts/splitTask.ts, scripts/taskGroups.ts, scripts/tackle-tasks-v1_1_SkillBodyEmitter.ts) that a reorg must also account for.

hooks/hooks.json names 9 distinct scripts/*.ts command paths: viewTaskHook.ts, readFileHook.ts, runStepHook.ts, taskStatsHook.ts, turn-modified-flag.ts, reflow-comments-post.ts, relatedTests.ts, stage-and-summarize-stop.ts, session-end-cleanup.ts. Each must keep resolving after the move.

Three runtime path computations build script paths as strings, so a move breaks them even with a green typecheck: scripts/prepareTasks.ts:84 (resolveMergeScriptPath), scripts/prepareTasks.ts:103 (resolveMergePhaseScriptPath), and scripts/reviewPlanBrief.ts:7 (fileURLToPath sibling import of planReviewRuling.ts).

scripts/taskStatsBrief.ts no longer exists; it was deleted in commit 284aa0e. Its successor, scripts/taskStatsHook.ts, uses a plain relative import, not a fileURLToPath computation, so it is not on the fragile-path list above.

This task moves close to 96+ files across every skill. The files array below cannot fence a move that size, so this task must be executed manually, outside the tackle-tasks fence system. The planner and implementer should still treat scripts/, tests/, skills/, and hooks/ as in scope.
tests: Add tests/scriptReferences.test.ts as a no-dangling-reference sweep: walk every command string in hooks/hooks.json, every `!` command line in skills/**/SKILL.md, and every relative import specifier in scripts/ and tests/, resolve each to an absolute path, and assert the file exists. The test must fail against a deliberately broken path, not pass vacuously when a glob matches nothing. Also assert resolveMergeScriptPath() and resolveMergePhaseScriptPath() point at existing files, and that the sibling URL resolved in scripts/reviewPlanBrief.ts exists. Alongside it, the full existing suite and the typecheck must stay green.

title: Give the codex plan reviewer the sibling-task and blocker scope so chain boundaries are not flagged as omissions
userDescription: verify.workflow.js should pass sibling-task scope (tasks owning overlapping files, plus the blockedBy graph) into the reviewer prompt, so codex stops flagging deliberate chain boundaries as omissions.
goal: - run-arguments.json carries a blockedBy array for every task that declares one
- the reviewer prompt names each sibling task sharing the group's files, by number and title
- the reviewer prompt states which tasks block, and are blocked by, the task under review
- a plan that leaves work to a named sibling or blocker is approved, not rejected as an omission
description:
The plan reviewer prompt (planReviewPrompt in scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/CodexReviewBodyEmitter.ts) only lists file paths. It never names the tasks that share files with the task under review, and never names the task's blockedBy entries. So codex reports work owned by a sibling or a blocker as an omission.

Sibling scope comes from groupTasksByFileOverlap in scripts/taskGroups.ts (overlap on modifiableFiles). Blockers come from the task record's blockedBy array (entry key taskNumber, see scripts/checkBlockers.ts). loadPreparedTask in scripts/tackle-tasks/shared/preparedTask.ts reads neither today.

Add siblingTasks (number + title) and blockedBy to PreparedTask. Have planReviewPrompt print both lists and state plainly: work assigned to a named sibling or blocker is out of scope and must not be reported as an omission. Task 120 (closed) already tells the reviewer what is not grounds for rejection. This task supplies the scope facts that make that judgement possible.
tests: In tests/prepareTasks.test.ts assert buildWorkflowArguments carries blockedBy through. In a verify-workflow test, build fake ARGS with two same-group tasks and assert codexPrompt names the sibling and the blocker.
problemSolvedByTask: Codex needs to know if other tasks are related to the plan being reviewed, which might explain some of the plan's omissions found by codex, so that codex doesn't reject a plan for a reason that another task is meant to solve.

title: Backfill goal and chainGoal on every open task in tasks.json
userDescription: yes, create a task to backfill goals for tasks in tasks.json.  completedTasks.json is excluded.
goal: - every task in .taskTools/tasks.json carries a non-empty goal array; completedTasks.json is untouched
- tasks that belong to a chain share one identical chainGoal array across that chain
- a test asserts the every-open-task-has-a-goal invariant and fails when a task lacks one
- each goal entry is one line with no embedded newline, and every task carries a notInScope array
notInScope: - rewriting or shortening existing description text is NOT in scope; that is task 116
description:
Measured against the current file: 12 open tasks; 2 without a goal (36, 113); 10 tasks declare a non-empty blockedBy; 0 tasks carry chainGoal. The 131-153 pipeline chain referenced in the original description no longer exists in tasks.json. Expect roughly 2 rounds of per-task authoring, not 40.

The user chose per-task authoring: settle each goal through AskUserQuestion before writing it, as createTaskBrief instructs, rather than drafting in bulk and reviewing in batches.

Format is fixed by work already landed: goal and chainGoal are arrays of strings, one line per entry, joined by goalText in scripts/taskFiles.ts and rendered by writeTaskBriefFile under "## Chain goal" and "## Goal". Do not re-emit the "This task is considered done when all of these are true:" heading — the brief prints it.

One caveat the user accepted: the invariant test fails the moment any task is added without a goal. createTaskBrief now always instructs a goal, so the invariant should hold, but a mid-run task written by another path will break the suite.

Before goals can be written for each remaining open task, each needs either a direct interview with the user, or a deep dive into its historical transcript_path to find the conversation where the task was created and derive the context that led to it — a goal drafted from the description alone risks missing scope the original conversation actually decided.
tests: Add a test that reads tasks.json and asserts every open task has a non-empty goal array.
problemSolvedByTask: Without a goal array, nobody (human or planner agent) can tell when a task is actually done versus merely touched.

title: 'changes detected' Stop hook prints the real staged diff
userDescription: make the 'changes detected' hook print out what changes are actually staged, because the agent's view of staged changes is always stale.  It should use the same code that the commit-message hook uses to provide the list of staged changes.
goal: - After a turn that edits and stages a file, the Stop hook's additionalContext contains the actual `git diff --staged` text for that file, not only the generic 'Files were changed' sentence.
- The staged-diff text comes from the same scripts/stagedDiffs.ts code path the commit-message skill uses; no second copy of the diff logic exists in the repo.
- The full diff is emitted, not a file-name-only list.
- Staged changes in a submodule whose pointer moved appear in the hook output, labelled per repo, the same way the commit-message skill labels them.
- `npm test` passes, including an updated tests/stage-and-summarize-stop.test.ts that asserts the staged-diff text is present in additionalContext.
notInScope: - NOT in scope: changing the commit-message skill's own output or wording, changing the EXCLUDES list in stagedDiffs.ts, and changing the staging behaviour itself -- the hook still only reports, it never stages.
description:
The 'changes detected' hook is scripts/stage-and-summarize-stop.ts (Stop/SubagentStop), which currently only checks `git status --porcelain` column two per file to decide if anything is unstaged, then emits a generic additionalContext string 'Files were changed. Stage the changes...' with no diff content. The commit-message skill already has the reusable staged-diff code in scripts/stagedDiffs.ts: it resolves the repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from `process.cwd()`, runs `git diff --staged` with an EXCLUDES filter, and recurses into any submodule whose pointer moved. Note stagedDiffs.ts is currently a top-level script that writes to stdout, not an exported function -- confirm its actual shape in the source before assuming an export exists; extracting a reusable function is expected. stage-and-summarize-stop.ts must call that shared code and include the actual staged-diff text in the additionalContext payload instead of the generic reminder, so the agent sees what is really staged rather than trusting its stale in-context view. The user chose the FULL staged diff, not a file-name-only list, and chose reuse of the same code over a new lighter implementation. Complication: stage-and-summarize-stop.ts iterates over `paths` that can span multiple repos/submodules (using `dirname(p)` per path), while stagedDiffs.ts resolves only one repo root from cwd with no repo parameter, so this task must either loop the stagedDiffs logic per distinct repo root among the flagged paths, or add a repo-path parameter. tests/stage-and-summarize-stop.test.ts's `run()` helper currently asserts additionalContext matches /commit-message skill/ and does not exercise diff content, so the tests need updating to assert the emitted diff text appears in additionalContext.

## Audit correction (2026-08-31)

scripts/stagedDiffs.ts already exports stagedDiffs() (line 27) with a CLI guard at line 55 — the extraction this description asks to confirm is done. It takes no repo argument and resolves a single root from cwd; the remaining work is the repo-path parameter. 'The hook still only reports, it never stages' means not in scope for this task; task 160 owns staging behavior.
tests: Unit test on the hook: create a temp git repo, write and `git add` a file, feed scripts/stage-and-summarize-stop.ts its Stop-hook JSON on stdin (with a turn-flag file listing that path), and assert the printed hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext contains the staged diff text for that file.
problemSolvedByTask: The agent doesn't accurately see what is really staged after the end-of-turn stage-and-summarize-stop.ts hook fires.

title: Add a /mermaid skill that diagrams a codebase into a .mmd file
userDescription: make a '/mermaid' skill that searches a codebase and builds a .mmd mermaid diagram.  it should follow the same mermaid diagram rules that I used for the diagrams in taskTools-86 (Yes/No boxes at decision points, output boxes -> what gets outputted, etc)
goal: - A /mermaid skill exists at skills/mermaid/SKILL.md and appears in the skill list.
- Running /mermaid against a codebase writes a .mmd file the user can name and open.

- The written .mmd follows the diagrams/tackle-tasks grammar: flowchart TB, boxes declared inside subgraphs as BOX_ID["label"], edges written as A -- "label" --> B, decision boxes branch with two edges labeled YES and NO (never separate _YES/_NO boxes), a classDef/class block assigns every box a role, and cross-section targets are grouped in a "next diagram" subgraph joined by an invisible ~~~ link.
- The skill contains an explicit written checklist of those diagram rules, and the skill follows that checklist when it draws.
notInScope: - NOT in scope: changing any existing diagram in diagrams/tackle-tasks/, and changing scripts/generateSteps.ts. The skill only reads generateSteps.ts as the reference parser whose grammar its output must match; the skill's own output documents an arbitrary codebase and need not itself be runnable by generateSteps.ts.
description:
Add a new /mermaid skill (skills/mermaid/SKILL.md, following the existing skill format seen in skills/view-task/SKILL.md and skills/create-task/SKILL.md) that searches a target codebase and emits a .mmd mermaid flowchart. It must codify the diagramming grammar already used in diagrams/tackle-tasks/*.mmd and parsed by scripts/generateSteps.ts (see getEdgesInDiagram and getPromptBoxesInDiagram, roughly lines 60-120, and the `returns_a_prompt` class-role check at line 111 (`getPromptBoxesInDiagram`)): `flowchart TB`, boxes declared inside a named `subgraph ... end` block as `BOX_ID["label"]` (a decision box is a plain rectangular box whose id ends in `_Q`, not a diamond node), edges written `A -- "label" --> B` or `A --> B`, decision boxes branching with two edges whose labels are literally `YES` and `NO` (extra detail can follow on a `
` line) rather than separate `_YES`/`_NO` boxes, a `classDef`/`class` block at the end assigning every box exactly one role among `script`, `returns_a_prompt`, `next_diagram`, `output`, and `fail`, and any box the diagram references but does not itself resolve grouped into a second `subgraph ... ["next diagram"]` block joined to the main subgraph by an invisible `~~~` link. Reference examples: diagrams/tackle-tasks/pipeline-planTheTask.mmd, diagrams/tackle-tasks/pipeline-whatIsReviewVerdict.mmd, and diagrams/tackle-tasks/pipeline-preambleStatusCheck.mmd. No existing skill in skills/ produces diagrams; this is a new skill directory, not an edit to an existing one. The skill must also carry an explicit written checklist of these diagram rules that it follows while it draws. The /mermaid skill documents codebases generally, not just taskTools pipelines, so its output does not need to be runnable by generateSteps.ts (which is hardcoded to the tackle-tasks box-ownership map) — it only needs to follow the same grammar.
tests: skip -- generateSteps.ts is hardcoded to the tackle-tasks pipeline's box-ownership map (BLOCKS_BY_OWNER_FOLDER) and its cross-diagram remapping, so it cannot run as a general-purpose grammar validator against a diagram of an arbitrary codebase. Acceptance is checked against the written checklist inside the skill itself (every box declared in a subgraph, every edge label cosmetic, every box assigned a class, decision boxes branch on YES/NO edge labels) rather than a runnable script.
problemSolvedByTask: Understanding an unfamiliar codebase's control flow means reading files by hand — no automated way to get a flowchart.

title: Read the diagram folder for tackle-tasks from .taskTools/settings.json
userDescription: The ability to define which set of diagrams to use for tackle-tasks.  this ability makes the skill and pipeline runner generic, allowing the end user to provide their own diagrams.  the default diagram would be the current pipeline.  .taskTools/settings.json is where this diagram setting would live.
goal: - With no .taskTools/settings.json, `/tackle-tasks [N]` runs the current pipeline block for block: the run-log's ran[] matches today's.
- With settings.json holding `{ "diagramFolder": "<path>" }`, generateSteps, the workflow and the hook all read that folder; the run-log names that folder's blocks and none of the default pipeline's.
- A diagramFolder that does not exist or holds no .mmd stops the run at launch with a message naming the path. No fallback.
notInScope: - Not in scope: a guide for users who author their own diagrams. A later task owns it.
description:
generateSteps.ts (invoked as `node scripts/generateSteps.ts diagrams/tackle-tasks` from package.json's "steps"/"steps:watch" scripts) resolves the diagram folder from process.argv, falling back to the dead default `plans/diagrams` (diagrams actually live at diagrams/tackle-tasks/*.mmd) when no CLI arg is given. It walks that folder into scripts/steps.json plus per-box stub scripts under scripts/tackle-tasks/, using a hardcoded BLOCKS_BY_OWNER_FOLDER box-name map tied to the current pipeline's diagram set. generateWorkflow.ts and runStepHook.ts consume the already-generated scripts/steps.json and are diagram-folder-agnostic, so they don't need to change. No .taskTools/settings.json file or reader exists anywhere in the codebase yet (grepped scripts/, skills/, tests/) — this would be a new config file and a new settings-read helper, most naturally added in generateSteps.ts's CLI entrypoint (diagramFolder resolution) ahead of its current argv/hardcoded-default fallback, with the current diagrams/tackle-tasks folder becoming the default when no setting is present.

Setting shape settled with the user: `{ "diagramFolder": "<path>" }`. The folder holds the .mmd files plus each block's script and template. An absent file or key means diagrams/tackle-tasks.

## Audit correction (2026-08-31)

User decision: both step consumers stay in the fence. scripts/runStepHook.ts and scripts/generateWorkflow.ts are owned so the merge fence cannot block this task, whichever consumer ends up edited. The setting may still flow only through regenerated scripts/steps.json (also owned), in which case the hook and workflow generator need no code change.
tests: A test writes .taskTools/settings.json naming a temp folder with one .mmd of two blocks and their scripts; runs /tackle-tasks; asserts the hook walked those two blocks and none of the default pipeline.
problemSolvedByTask: The user cannot provide their own pipeline (mermaid diagram) for how they want tasks completed. sometimes the current pipeline is too complex/uses too many agents.

title: Add plain-node query script over tasks.json for blockers and file matches
userDescription: Add one query script over .taskTools/tasks.json that answers two questions with no agent and no database: "what blocks task N" (follow the blockedBy chain, print each blocker's taskNumber, title, and reason) and "which open tasks touch file X" (match X against each open task's modifiableFiles). Reads tasks.json directly with node; no SQLite, no new dependency. This replaces task 188 (closed 2026-09-02 as not relevant; see plans/decision-sqlite-task-storage.md). Difficulty 2. One test that seeds a small fixture tasks.json and asserts both answers.
goal: - `node scripts/queryTasks.ts blockers N` prints each blocker's taskNumber, title, and reason, following the blockedBy chain, with no agent run
- `node scripts/queryTasks.ts files X` prints every open task whose modifiableFiles contains X
- The script reads .taskTools/tasks.json only; no SQLite, no new dependency in package.json
problemSolvedByTask: extracting information from tasks.json requires complex 'jq' expressions, vs. simpler SQL queries and table joins.
description: tasks.json is a flat array of TaskRecord objects (scripts/taskFiles.ts, readTaskFile) each with taskNumber, title, files, and blockedBy: {taskNumber, reason}[] (buildTaskEntry in scripts/appendTask.ts writes blockedBy entries keyed taskNumber, but existing rows in tasks.json/completedTasks.json use the older key taskNum — the script must check both keys or it silently reports an empty blocker chain). scripts/checkBlockers.ts already does an in-memory blockedBy walk with cycle protection over openTasks; the new script's blocker-chain walk can follow the same shape but should not depend on checkBlockers' open-only filtering, since a blocker can be closed. scripts/getTaskDetails.ts (readTaskLists) shows the existing helper for loading tasks.json/completedTasks.json arrays and can be reused for reading. Add a new standalone script, e.g. scripts/queryTasks.ts, invoked directly with node — no agent, no SQLite, no new dependency.
tests: Write a small fixture tasks.json with 3 tasks (A blocked by B, B blocked by C; A and C touch scripts/foo.ts). Run the script for 'what blocks A' and assert B and C print with title and reason. Run 'which tasks touch scripts/foo.ts' and assert A and C print.
notInScope: - Moving tasks to a database — task 188 was closed on 2026-09-02 and nothing owns that now
